pamphlet_excerpts: Unexpected Programming Injuries: You might not think that writing programs could cause injuries (p. 88).
Athletic Prevention Techniques: But in fact, injuries from programming have much in common with sports injuries and can be prevented using some of the same techniques that athletes use (p. 88).
Repetitive Stress Injuries: The main programming-related injuries are repetitive stress injuries, or RSIs (p. 88).
Joint and Tendon Stress: Just as in athletic activities, an RSI occurs when stress is placed on a joint, pulling on the tendons and muscles around the joint (p. 88).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Identify Repetitive Stress: The main programming-related injuries are repetitive stress injuries, or RSIs (p. 88).
Step 2 - Protect Joints and Tendons: Just as in athletic activities, an RSI occurs when stress is placed on a joint, pulling on the tendons and muscles around the joint (p. 88).
Step 3 - Allow Tissue Recovery Time: When the stress happens repeatedly, the body does not have time to recover and becomes irritated (p. 88).
Step 4 - Monitor Swelling and Irritation: The body reacts to the irritation by increasing the amount of fluid in that area to reduce the stress placed on the tendon or muscle (p. 88).

Mid-Century Language Pioneers: By the 1950s and 1960s, many new languages were being introduced, including BASIC, Fortran, and LISP (p. 18).
Moving Beyond Machine Assembly: These languages took programming beyond binary and assembly to allow portability of languages beyond just the processor hardware of the time (p. 18).
Cross-Platform Program Portability: That is, programs written in these languages could runon two or more kinds of processors or with two or more kinds of operating systems (p. 18).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Trace Early Assembly Roots: These languages took programming beyond binary and assembly to allow portability of languages beyond just the processor hardware of the time (p. 18).
Step 2 - Compare Cross-Platform Portability: That is, programs written in these languages could runon two or more kinds of processors or with two or more kinds of operating systems (p. 18).
Step 3 - Examine Computer Science Concepts: Many languages, such as Pascal, we recreated to capture new concepts of computer science (p. 18).
Step 4 - Match Languages to Industries: Others, such as Fortran and COBOL, were developed to meet specific needs of science or business (p. 18).

options: A. They eliminated the need for a central processing unit inside the computer.
B. They allowed programs to be portable across multiple types of processors and operating systems.
C. They restricted software so it could only run on one custom-built mainframe processor.
D. They replaced all mathematical operations with spoken voice commands.
choices: A. They eliminated the need for a central processing unit inside the computer.
B. They allowed programs to be portable across multiple types of processors and operating systems.
C. They restricted software so it could only run on one custom-built mainframe processor.
D. They replaced all mathematical operations with spoken voice commands.
quiz_item.correct_answer: B. They allowed programs to be portable across multiple types of processors and operating systems.
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (B): High-level languages took programming beyond hardware-specific binary and assembly, enabling programs to run on two or more processor types or operating systems (p. 18).

options: A. Work in a dark room without breaks to maintain focus, and remove copyright headers from open-source files so your repository looks uniform.
B. Hold your wrists bent upward against the desk edge, and copy proprietary source code from commercial apps as long as your program is free.
C. Sit with the monitor 6 inches from your eyes, and assume any code posted on a public forum is in the public domain.
D. Maintain neutral wrist and back posture, follow the 20-20-20 rule to prevent eye strain, and respect software licenses by keeping required open-source attributions.
choices: A. Work in a dark room without breaks to maintain focus, and remove copyright headers from open-source files so your repository looks uniform.
B. Hold your wrists bent upward against the desk edge, and copy proprietary source code from commercial apps as long as your program is free.
C. Sit with the monitor 6 inches from your eyes, and assume any code posted on a public forum is in the public domain.
D. Maintain neutral wrist and back posture, follow the 20-20-20 rule to prevent eye strain, and respect software licenses by keeping required open-source attributions.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: D. Maintain neutral wrist and back posture, follow the 20-20-20 rule to prevent eye strain, and respect software licenses by keeping required open-source attributions.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (D): Safe programming combines ergonomic posture and regular 20-20-20 visual breaks with ethical adherence to open-source and commercial software licensing rules.

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: What major advantage did 1950s and 1960s languages like BASIC, Fortran, and LISP introduce over earlier binary and assembly coding?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: What major advantage did 1950s and 1960s languages like BASIC, Fortran, and LISP introduce over earlier binary and assembly coding?
options: A. They eliminated the need for a central processing unit inside the computer.
B. They allowed programs to be portable across multiple types of processors and operating systems.
C. They restricted software so it could only run on one custom-built mainframe processor.
D. They replaced all mathematical operations with spoken voice commands.
choices: A. They eliminated the need for a central processing unit inside the computer.
B. They allowed programs to be portable across multiple types of processors and operating systems.
C. They restricted software so it could only run on one custom-built mainframe processor.
D. They replaced all mathematical operations with spoken voice commands.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. They allowed programs to be portable across multiple types of processors and operating systems.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): High-level languages took programming beyond hardware-specific binary and assembly, enabling programs to run on two or more processor types or operating systems (p. 18).

D. Mobile devices can only execute programs written in 1950s punch-card Fortran.
choices: A. Mobile applications must be wired directly into the battery with a soldering iron.
B. Mobile applications cannot use loops, variables, or conditional statements.
C. The mobile operating system is designed as a framework within which apps are built and run.
D. Mobile devices can only execute programs written in 1950s punch-card Fortran.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: C. The mobile operating system is designed as a framework within which apps are built and run.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): Most mobile applications differ from traditional programming because the mobile operating system is designed as a framework that manages app life cycle and device features (p. 35).
